text:
ConocoPhillips rose modestly today as oil prices remained elevated, with U.S. crude holding above $101 per barrel and world oil trading significantly higher at $126.55. The stock has climbed steadily over the past two weeks (up 12.68%), tracking a surge in oil driven by ongoing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian and shipping infrastructure in the Middle East — developments that have kept supply concerns alive despite some optimism about diplomatic progress.

The wide gap between U.S. and world oil prices ($24.64 per barrel difference) reflects these geopolitical tensions affecting global crude supply, while the U.S. market benefits from its own production. As a major oil and gas producer, ConocoPhillips tends to track crude prices closely, so the persistence of elevated global oil has supported the stock's gains even as today's individual move was small.
